name: Behavior-Expanding TAM Scenarios

positioning.oneLineSummary: Tests whether product improvements create new frequency, price points, coverage, or use cases that expand demand beyond a historical category.
positioning.productLabel: Behavior-Expanding TAM Scenario Lens — based on Bill Gurley's public market-size analysis
notAClaimOf: one company capturing all category expansion
a portfolio-company case being a universal template

attribution.display: Based on Bill Gurley's public Above the Crowd market-size analysis

neutralParaphrase: When a product materially changes experience, price, reliability, coverage, frequency, or use cases, model the possibility that demand expands beyond historical category spend. Use multiple explicit scenarios and current behavior rather than a single heroic TAM.

locator.value: Lines 19-76: historical-category assumption, product deltas, new use cases, scenario ranges, regulation, competition, and network effects
Factors 6-8: addressable penetration, market expansion, and frequency
2011-05-26 update on TAM and optionality; revenue alone remains a poor valuation guide

requiredConditions: The company claims a material product delta from the historical alternative.
Changed behavior can be measured or tested.
Conflict and survivorship bias in the source case are disclosed.

requiredEvidence.description: Prior category spend, behavior, frequency, price, coverage, substitutes, and non-consumption.
Measured change in price, time, reliability, convenience, quality, coverage, or workflow.
New users, greater frequency, new use cases, substitution, willingness to pay, and cohort persistence.
Regulation, competition, local network limits, supply, capital, price elasticity, and the company's plausible capture share.

decisionQuestions: Which product delta changes behavior rather than merely share?
Who becomes a new user and which new use case appears?
How persistent is the increase in frequency or spend?
How much demand is substitution versus category expansion?
What regulation, competition, supply, or local-network constraint limits company capture?
positiveSignals: Observed cohorts show persistent new use cases or higher frequency.
Non-consumers enter because a specific friction falls.
Independent scenario inputs and company data converge.
Bear, base, and bull cases separate category expansion from company share.
redFlags: The company relabels adjacent spend as TAM without behavior evidence.
One portfolio success or analogy supplies the entire expansion assumption.
The bull case is presented as base case.
Constraints and competitor capture are omitted.
disconfirmingEvidence: A better product can mostly redistribute existing spend.
Early heavy users may not represent a broader population.
Lower price can increase units while limiting revenue and contribution.
Incumbents or other entrants may capture much of the expanded category.
contraindications: Do not use one deterministic expanded-TAM number.
Do not hide source conflict or portfolio exposure.
Do not convert expanded TAM directly into value without economics, share, and price.

instructions: Establish historical behavior and product delta.
Measure new-user, frequency, use-case, and substitution evidence.
Construct bear, base, and bull expansion scenarios deterministically.
Apply constraints and plausible company capture separately.
Conclude observed expansion, plausible but early, share-shift only, overstated, or insufficient.

deterministicRule.serviceBoundary: TAM scenarios, penetration, frequency, price, substitution, and company-share calculations must be computed outside the language model.

sourceReliability.high: Longitudinal behavior, transaction, and independent market evidence converge.

evidenceStrength.high: Persistent multi-cohort expansion survives price and constraint tests.

evidenceCoverage.high: Substitution, scenarios, constraints, capture, economics, and counterevidence covered.

applicabilityConfidence.high: Market expansion is central to underwriting.

judgmentConfidence.high: Observed behavior and independent data support a calibrated range.

empiricalQualifications: Market expansion forecasts have severe uncertainty.
Portfolio-company examples are selected and conflicted.

rights.notes: Public case analysis is neutrally paraphrased with conflict caveat.

openIssues: Define substitution and behavior-expansion evidence standards.
